page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a catchword-like signature line "AMOR" at lower right; no margin notes. Running head at top centre; page number top left.

main_text.p: Amantes quei soleant affectus suos exprimere, quibus gestibus ac factis, graphicè depingit amasia adolescentis. Pseud. 1. 1. v. 62. & seqq.
Quod amamus, osculari licet. Merc. 3. 3. v. 12.
Senem osculari mulierem turpe est. Ib. v. 13. Quia nimirum vomitum excutit mulieri. Ibid. Ideò Vervece dicti. Ibid.
Adolescentes quasi religioni sibi ducunt, amicæ maledicere, & minari. Bacch. 3. 4. v. 5.
Amorum conciliatrix est Venus. Mil. 4. 6. v. 12. Illam adorabant ut propitiam sibi. Ib. v. 15.
Amatores in foro stabant. Capt. 3. 1. v. 18.
Amor vetus non tamen obsolescit. Cistell. 1. 1. v. III.
Amoris comes egestas. Pseud. 1. 3. v. 38. Quid agitur? C A. amatur, atq; egetur acriter.
In amore dona sint oportet. Most. 1. 3. v. 28.
Matronæ, non meretricium est, unum infervire amantem. Most. 1. 3. v. 33.
Amatores solent esse cavillatores faceti, commodi convivæ. Mil. 3. 1. v. 46.
Amatores vovebant mane Veneri jentaculum. Curc. 1. 1. v. 72.
Non decet senes amare, sed adolescentes. Merc. 5. 4. v. 23. 25. 27. Vide etiam Tit. Adulteri.
Non vestem amatores mulieris amant, sed vestis fartum: h.e. corpus ipsum, quod in veste. Most. 1. 3. v. 13.
Amoris arrhabonem annulum dabant. Mil. 4. 1. v. 11.
Amantes Oculum appellabant amicas suas. Most. 1. 3. v. 152. Vide Lex. Plaut.
Amor multos illexit in dispendium. Merc.Prol. v. 53.
Amantes non possunt pati suas ab alijs basiari. Mortem potius volunt. Truc. 5. v. 34.

page.notes: Page is a printed page of the Electa Plautina index; left margin is empty of notes. Some italic references and Greek/Latin words are approximate; the printed Roman numerals in the cited references were read as printed where legible. The text "Alte sich wohl nicht" in German black letter appears beside the line "Amor vetus non tamen obsolescit" and is not transcribed, as it could not be read reliably.
